current authoritative evidence without warning. We study when this harm begins
as model capability changes. We evaluate a frozen, closed-set, action-scored

evidence.excerpt:
Because "no memory" has 2 incompatible meanings here, we split the benchmark into 2 suites. In
the Benefit suite (A) the task is unsolvable without the stored fact ("book my usual airline"); no
current context is present, so the no-memory baseline is floored at chance and the harm of interest is
over-trusting a stale stored fact. In the Safety suite (B) an authoritative tool holds the correct value in
every condition, so the no-memory baseline is ceilinged; here we can measure net harm, which is
following a stale memory over the current authoritative value and so dropping accuracy below not
having the memory at all.
Table 1 makes the design concrete with a single Safety-suite scenario: an authoritative calendar tool
always holds the correct room, and the stored memory is what varies across the 4 conditions defined
next. The Benefit-suite version of the same task simply omits the tool,

Abase scenariois a single templated situation with a fixed ground-truth action and slot values (the
room booking in Table 1 is one); scenarios that share a template but draw different slot values from a
curated pool (other rooms, users, or tools) form atemplate family. The frozen benchmark (v1) has
300 base scenarios (150 per suite), expanded from a 56-scenario pilot by a deterministic curated-pool
generator and pinned by SHA-256 with a manifest; the 150 scenarios per suite span 33 template
families (the resampling unit for the cluster bootstrap in §5). Before freezing, the authors manually
reviewed all 300 base scenarios, reading each to confirm a single unambiguous, tool-consistent
ground-truth action, correct suite and condition assignment, and the absence of harmful or sensitive
content.

evidence.excerpt:
Each item produces a constrained action. We score the action using an exact, regex, or canonical
match against the construction-time ground truth (no LLM judge), manually validated against human
reading on a random sample of outputs. The benchmark uses 4 conditions: no_memory (baseline,
floored in the Benefit suite, ceilinged in Safety), clean (memory agrees with the truth; the upper
bound), stale (memory holds an outdated value; the harm condition), and explicit_conflict
(the stale and correct values are both stored; an adjudication stress test). To remove any position
prior over the answer options we usecircular option-permutation averaging( noptions=3, chance
≈0.33 ): each scenario is scored under every cyclic rotation of its options and averaged before any
comparison.

evidence.excerpt:
In the Safety suite the no-memory baseline is preserved (no-mem ≥0.98 in every cell), so any
negative ∆mem is genuine net harm: the model follows a stale memory over an authoritative tool.
We vary the conditions that make the stale note increasingly plausible (levels L0–L3, e.g. inflating
its apparent recency) and report ρ∗ as the first significant level rather than fitting a continuous
relationship (Figure 2, Table 3). The 0.6B model crosses into significant net harm already at L0,
whereas 1.7B/4B/8B first cross at L1: ρ∗ = 0/1/1/1. The threshold therefore separates the 0.6B
model from the other 3 models; it does not produce a monotone ordering by capability.
At the higher recency-inflated levels, the size ordering changes. At L3, the 8B model has reliance
1.00 and ∆mem −1.00; at L2, the 4B model has reliance 0.83. Making the stale note appear newer
4

Overlapping or non-overlapping per-model intervals do not by themselves establish an interaction.
We therefore bootstrap paired differences between model sizes (Table 6). Recency is significantly
stronger on the larger models (8B−0.6B = +.302∗; mean(large)−mean(small) = +.333∗), position
significantly reverses (8B−0.6B =−.326 ∗), authority shows no interaction (ns), and the label feature
shows a null group contrast, which is why we call it universal rather than scale-growing. Two
robustness checks support the exploratory posture: a template-family cluster bootstrap (resampling
whole families) leaves every significant main effect significant, widening CIs only ×1.1–2.2 with
nothing crossing 0; and leave-one-family-out moves the Benefit-suite estimate by ≤0.012 at every
scale. The over-trust pattern reproduces on the capable sizes of an independent Llama-Instruct
model-size series (§7).

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims remain well-aligned with empirical evidence throughout the text, carefully distinguishing reliance behavior from paired net harm and clarifying that framing controls show the phenomenon is not strictly memory-specific.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation thoroughly supports the core claims, utilizing rigorous statistical uncertainty measures (95% percentile bootstrap intervals, template-family cluster bootstraps, and cross-size contrast tests). Findings are further validated using external benchmarks (RGB, MisBench), an independent model family (Llama-3.2/3.1), and ablation controls (framing and thinking mode).
primary.limitations: The authors transparently report key limitations, including the inability of the Benefit suite to measure net harm on explicit conflict, reliance on closed-set action evaluation, restricting primary scaling to single-family series up to 8B, and testing memory consumption rather than full end-to-end read/write systems.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is rigorous and well-specified, introducing a frozen 300-scenario benchmark pinned by SHA-256 with explicit separation of floored Benefit and ceilinged Safety suites. It systematically isolates memory features (label, recency, authority, position) using circular option permutations to eliminate positional priors, complemented by direct paired cross-size bootstraps and cluster robustness checks.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a robust, methodologically sound empirical analysis of agent memory vulnerabilities with exemplary experimental controls, clear separation of metric constructs, thorough statistical validation, and well-calibrated scientific claims.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper investigates the Memory Trust Gap in persistent-memory LLM agents, demonstrating how model capability shapes reliance on stale memories versus current authoritative evidence across two complementary benchmark suites (Benefit and Safety). Through a 2x2x2x2 factorial feature design and mitigation evaluations across model scales (Qwen3 0.6B to 8B, replicated on Llama-Instruct), it shows that stale-memory harm is capability-gated, feature triggers shift with scale, and effective mitigations depend on model size.
